transcript.text: Our Samsung combi microwave keeps whirring for a few minutes after it's finished and beeped, even with the door open. Old one never did that. Is the fan stuck on?

Yes, it is very likely the cooling fan staying on, which is normal behaviour to cool the magnetron after use, though it can sometimes indicate a stuck fan or a control issue if it runs much longer than usual. Since your old one didn't do this, it could be a difference in design or a minor fault with the fan motor or its relay. To check if this is just standard operation for your model, try running a cup of water on full power for one minute and see how long the whirring continues after it stops cooking. If it runs for more than five minutes after cooling down, that suggests the fan might be stuck or the control board isn't cutting power to it correctly.

Ok, I can try that. Runs for a few minutes after, and it does eventually stop on its own. Longest after I've used the grill or oven mode, and after a short reheat it barely runs. Should I test the water thing anyway?

Yes, please go ahead and run the cup of water test to confirm if this is normal cooling behaviour for your specific model. It sounds like the fan is working as intended by running longer after high-heat modes like the grill, but since it still whirs with the door open, we should check if this is a standard feature or a fault. To be sure, could you please find the model number on the back of the microwave or inside the door frame? This will help me confirm if your Samsung combi is designed to run the fan for that duration after use. If you can't reach the label right now, we can wait until you have it handy.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I can't find the full model number, I only know it starts MC28. Is that enough to go on? I'll do the water test too.

Yes, knowing it starts with MC28 is enough for me to give you some specific advice. The behaviour you are describing—running longer after grill or oven modes—is typical for combi microwaves because those functions generate significant heat that needs to be dissipated. Since the fan eventually stops on its own and doesn't run after a simple reheat, it suggests the cooling system is working as intended rather than being stuck in an error state. To confirm this is normal operation for your specific model, please go ahead with the water test you mentioned; if the fan runs for about 2-3 minutes after that short cook and then stops, it is likely just standard thermal management.

Just did the water test. The fan ran for a few minutes after the beep and then stopped on its own. The manual also says the fan may operate after cooking to cool the oven, so does that mean it's normal?

Yes, that suggests it is normal behaviour for your Samsung MC28 combi microwave. The fan running for a few minutes after cooking, especially following high-heat modes like the grill or oven, is designed to cool down internal components and protect the magnetron. Since it stops on its own and doesn't run unnecessarily after short tasks like reheating, there is no fault with the fan or the control system. You can continue using your appliance as usual without any concerns.
